# Animations {.unnumbered}

*This chapter shows the kinds of movie the toolkit produces — a quick way to see
what the coupled model resolves — and how to make them.*

The animation scripts live in
[`analytics/animations/`](../../../analytics/animations/) and share a single
engine, **`animlib.py`**. They serve a range of work (tracer transport, oxygen
dynamics, nitrogen-budget diagnostics), so they sit in one shared place rather
than inside any single analysis package.

## The shared engine

`animlib.py` (formerly `animate_oxy_diags.py`) provides the reusable machinery:
hgrid reading with the `tri_to_elem` element→triangle mapping; node- vs
element-centred rendering; dry-cell masking (`dryFlagNode` / `dryFlagElement`);
fill-value masking (AED's `9.97e36` sentinel → NaN); multi-stack
auto-discovery; the gliding time-series inset; and the FFmpeg writer. It is also
runnable standalone as a configurable multi-panel animator.

## The scripts

| Script | Animates |
|---|---|
| `animlib.py` | configurable multi-panel (scribe vars + AED diagnostics) |
| `animate_oxy.py` | single tracer (1–2 panel); legacy standalone |
| `animate_O2fluxes.py` | OXY_oxy + O2 atmospheric / sediment fluxes |
| `animate_Nfluxes.py` | 6-panel nitrogen sediment / atmospheric flux sheets |
| `animate_Nrates.py` | 6-panel 3D nitrogen process rates |
| `animate_STO2.py` | salinity + temperature + oxygen |
| `animate_velocity.py` | depth velocity magnitude |
| `animate_trc.py` | full-domain conservative tracers TRC_tr1/2/3 |
| `animate_trc_zoomed.py` | Pioneer-mouth TRC plume + transect overlay |
| `upper_river_connectivity_animation.py` | upper-river wet/dry connectivity |

## Running

Most scripts share the same flags (`--hgrid`, `--outputs-dir`, `--fps`,
`--dpi`, `--xlim/--ylim`, `--ndays`, `--single-stack`, `--n-stacks`, `--layer`):

```bash
python animate_Nfluxes.py --outputs-dir <run>/outputs --hgrid <run>/hgrid.gr3
python animlib.py --diag-vars OXY_sat NIT_nitrif --aed-cmb <run>/outputs/aed_data_cmb_1.nc
```

Two scripts depend on the budget packages and self-bootstrap their paths:
`animate_trc_zoomed.py` uses the generic `core` framework and the Pioneer
`run_config` (so it honours `--run 002|003`), and
`upper_river_connectivity_animation.py` uses `core`.

::: {.callout-tip}
Full-resolution `.mp4` renders are git-ignored; only the small web versions used
in this guide are committed under `docs/quarto/assets/videos/`.
:::
